column2: A unique alpha-numeric identification code assigned to each food. The key remains the same for each equivalent food across our food composition publications, allowing easy comparison of food profiles across datasets.
2-, 3-, or 5-digit numeric classification code which aligns with those used in the AUSNUT 2023 dataset.
Indicates how the majority of nutrient data, or data for key nutrients, were sourced. The derivations used in the Australian Food Composition Database are:

column3: Data generated by scientific analysis at a laboratory. May be commissioned by FSANZ or provided by a research organisation or the food industry.
Data is derived using a calculation based on the proportion of ingredients and cooking or preparation processes.
Data is based on a similar food, with only minor changes to relevant components.
Key data is derived from product information (online or on-pack) for Australian foods such as the Nutrition Information Panel (NIP) and ingredient lists.
Data is derived from international food composition databases.

column2: Although each food is assigned an overall derivation code, individual nutrient values may have been derived using different techniques. To assist in understanding the derivations, the source of data for individual components is provided in the sampling details.

A semi-structured naming system which highlights the key features of each food. In general, the food name captures:
    •	   exceptions to the most commonly available form of a food e.g. intense sweetened or reduced fat
    •	   the addition of vitamins and/or minerals for fortification purposes. For food which is always supplied in a fortified form, such as bread-making flour, this information is only included in the food description.
Provides further information about the food, such as a details of its appearance, texture, common ingredients or preparation techniques.

Provides information about where the nutrient data comes from, such as the number of samples purchased for analysis, the date and place of purchase, and  whether the data were imputed or borrowed. This field may also highlight any specific issues with particular nutrient values, such as analytical problems and areas of uncertainty.

Used to calculate protein content. All foods with a derivation of 'Recipe' have been allocated a default nitrogen factor of zero, as individual nitrogen factors have been applied at the ingredient level.

Used to calculate mass of fatty acids based on total fat. All foods with a derivation of 'Recipe' have been allocated a default fat factor of zero, as individual fat factors have been applied at the ingredient level.

In this dataset, the specific gravity is the density of a liquid food relative to the density of water. As it is a ratio, specific gravity has no unit of measurement.

All solid foods have been allocated a default specific gravity of zero.
Describes the portion of the food that is typically eaten.
Describes the portion of the food that is typically not eaten.
